title: unMORE: Unsupervised Multi-Object Segmentation via Center-Boundary Reasoning
summary: Local inverse-gradient identity overstatement; regular-point repair verified, full algorithm and empirical effects unverified.

problems.title: Universal inverse-gradient scale identity lacks regularity/discretization conditions
problems.claim: Eq4 recovers maximum signed distance at any positive foreground pixel
problems.location: p4 Eq4, used to motivate p6 Eq6
assumptions: Positive foreground pixel at center; normalization D=2
problems.check: Continuum one-sided derivatives and exact finite-difference samples
problems.result: No derivative at center; central gradient zero, forward reciprocal norm sqrt2 instead of2
problems.counterevidence: Identity valid at regular points with unit distance gradient; appendix/release average gradients and regularize
problems.impact: Local universal wording/derivation overstatement; no demonstrated failure of averaged heuristic or empirical contribution
problems.correction: Restrict identity to differentiable unit-gradient points with common metric; no convergence repair proved

independent_verification.original_claim_and_location: Read original physical p4 signed/normalized distance Eqs2-4 and any-interior-pixel claim; inspected actual p6 Eq6 and boundary-motion discussion. Read AppendixA.3 p14 averages and adjusted steps, and named static update code.
independent_verification.operative_assumptions: A single square [-2,2]^2 has exact interior distance S=2-max(|x|,|y|), maximumD=2 and center f=1>0. The five sampled center/axis positions also have these distances to the square boundary pixels. No learned prediction error, overlapping object or non-Euclidean norm is needed.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Independently took left/right derivatives of f(x,0)=1-|x|/2 at0: +1/2 versus -1/2, so there is no continuum gradient. Fresh rational samples give central gradient(0,0) and forward gradient(-1/2,-1/2), whose reciprocal norm is sqrt2 rather thanD=2. At regular point(1,0), derivative(-1/2,0) restoresD=2.
independent_verification.alternatives_and_counterevidence: The continuum eikonal identity holds at regular points with unit distance gradient and common metric. Appendix averages and code smooth reciprocal denominators alter the actual operator; the example does not establish that selected border pixels encounter the singular center or that the averaged update fails.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for the local universal wording and discrete-gradient identity, with Eq6 motivation traced. Central empirical damage is unestablished; this is not reduced solely because a repair is short but because the actual averaged/stabilized algorithm is not the refuted pointwise identity.
independent_verification.repair_scope: Restrict to differentiable exact distance points with norm(grad S)=1 and D>0; then grad f=grad S/D proves the repair. No finite-difference exactness, safe-step or convergence guarantee follows.
independent_verification.correspondence_check: Static lines140-174 implement w/a+(1-w)/b, and Appendix Eqs7-8 followed by inverse imply1/(wa+(1-w)b), generally different. datasets.py has outward grid-center vectors; objectness_net.py prediction heads have final linear/signed outputs, so the prose sign and terminal-ReLU observations remain specification correspondence limits, not proved benchmark defects.
